confidence_notes: I ran four web searches. One found the RBA rate and three covered food and drink prices. The FX figure is the 18 Nov 2026 4.00pm AEST AUD/USD rate of 0.6720. The search summary said this figure matches the RBA's exchange-rate RSS feed, but I did not open the RBA page myself. Beer, coffee and the mid-range meal for two come from crowd-sourced cost-of-living figures. Numbeo gives about USD 2.98 for a pint, 3.87 for a cappuccino and 54 for a mid-range meal for two. Other aggregators give lower figures of about USD 1.65-3 for beer, 2.5-3.7 for a cappuccino and 25-37 for the meal, so I used blended mid-points. Inexpensive-meal estimates vary widely, from about USD 4.5 to 11, partly depending on whether a drink is included, so I used a mid-high value. I found no aggregated cocktail or wine prices. Two Mérida bars list cocktails or drinks from about 95-100 MXN, so I put a standard cocktail at about 110-130 MXN. Wine by the glass is based on its usual price relationship to beer in Mexico, about 2x, so treat it as uncertain. Accommodation anchors are general-knowledge estimates for a tourist-oriented colonial city in July, which is low or shoulder season and very hot. I did not search for or check any accommodation listings.
comparable_city_reasoning: Mid-sized Mexican colonial cities with steady tourist and expat demand, such as Oaxaca, Puebla and Guanajuato, priced below Mexico City and well below Caribbean resort areas like Cancún and Playa del Carmen. Mérida's historic-centre hostels and boutique three-star hotels match those comparables.
